newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soybean harvest still ahead of normal.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soybean harvest still ahead of normal.

text.p: Arkansas's soybean harvest remained ahead of normal as of Sunday, despite heavy rains in many parts of the state, accoridng to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Soybeans were 10 percent harvested, up from seven percent a week earlier and five percent a year ago and on average.
The crop was 21 percent mature, up from 11 percent last year and a five-year average of 12 percent.
Rice was 75 percent harvested, also ahead of last year's 70 percent and the average of 64 percent, with cotton 18 percent harvested versus 12 and 13 percent respectively.
"Bollrot was a serious problem in Lafayette county and was increasing in Pulaski county in many cotton fields," the report said.
Heavy rain caused lodging in rice fields in Monroe and Pulaski counties.
Corn harvesting was winding down in many areas and was 93 percent finished, up from last year's 92 percent and the average pace of 90 percent.
Wheat planting was reported in several counties and was five percent complete, up from two percent last year and a five-year average of four percent.
